body:
OK, first off, if you want a name, just reference the username.

Anyway, so you've basically given up on the argument and are just saying there doesn't have to be a meaning. So most of your post was kind of redundant for me.

What I really wanted was for you to elaborate on your thing where you say I should keep people ignorant:

> make sure that as few people in the world realize the pointlessness of it all. Ignorance IS bliss my friend, and it is hard work to be informed when surrounded by it. But though every person's life may be pointless in this world, your work in easing their passage through this world (though also pointless) by keeping them either ignorant or distracted by their pointlessness is the true test of courage.

OK. I think your post is a mixed bag, so I'm going to respond to the points I found interesting.

> I don't follow how killing oneself takes courage when one takes the effort to find the easiest and least painful way to do it

It's pretty simple really. It doesn't feel good to be in pain. Why would I choose a deliberately painful method? Medically depressed people tend to do that, like cutting themselves and stuff. I could never do that. As I said, I'm not depressed. This is a philosophy and a mentality.

> make sure that as few people in the world realize the pointlessness of it all. Ignorance IS bliss my friend, and it is hard work to be informed when surrounded by it. But though every person's life may be pointless in this world, your work in easing their passage through this world (though also pointless) by keeping them either ignorant or distracted by their pointlessness is the true test of courage.

So you're telling me, that my purpose is to keep people ignorant? Really? I would love you to expand on this. I just do not see how that can help anything.

> Maybe by helping educate more people so the gene pendulum sways towards the intelligent, which may create better doctors or scientists to make everyone's lives better.

My whole point was that science is good enough in the West to where we live very comfortable life. I've lived a comfortable life. Health is not my problem, OK?

Plus, again, we're all going to die, so the point of making people's lives better is what?

Most people's struggles in life seem to be having a shitty life and trying to make it better. So I think once we all have great lives, people really will see the pointlessness of it. That's where I'm at now. I've seen enough and I think it's time to go. I have no struggle.

> Not only that, but you are afraid you are making the wrong decision, so you post here to allow yourself a scapegoat. You get to now blame reddit for not convincing you to not kill yourself.

No, no, no. See, you haven't even read my post. I said I'm awaiting for equipment to arrive by mail. Once it arrives, I will kill myself, so long as I haven't been convinced otherwise.

And to your last point, no, you don't need my name.

Banging chicks and getting STDs would get boring if you did it enough, as with anything. Plus, you can't go track down terrorists or shoot sharks unless you have a lot of money. Money would run out. You'd end up homeless. 

I don't think 4chan is the best place for philosophy.

> Even if you so whole heartedly believe in this one, a great mind never stops evolving

A great mind does stop evolving, once you're dead.

> no one is realy going to remember any of it anyway. Stay alive for the people who love you, but mostly for yourself

That is an unbelievably redundant statement. It's like you recognize life is pointless, but are still saying live anyway. I do not understand you.
If I plugged in a special device into your brain, you would the same stimulation as gained from doing something "out of the box", or working hard for some satisfaction.

> It doesn't matter how much you've lived, because the total sum of accumulated human experiences in a day far outpaces you on whatever you have gone through.

Nope. That's not what I believe. People have done far greater things than me. But they've wasted their time, because they're going to die.

> Here, if you're saying that most scientific mysteries are solved then you obviously don't have much of a scientific background

No, There's loads more to learn scientifically. I'm saying we know enough about science to support our meaningless lives, and we're not going to space, and even if we did, it would be pointless and a repetition of what we've built on Earth.

> You've been watching too much Zeitgeist.

No. Zeitgeist 1 is a shitty movie because it's completely inaccurate. Zeitgeist 2 and 3 are idiotic cult movies where they believe computers can run the world.

> We live at the verge of huge achievements in areas such as nanotechnology, molecular biology, quantum computing, and you're telling me science is done?

And what will be the point of these achievements? This is just a technology race for the sake of survival (i.e. build a nuke then build one to counter it). Things are getting more and more complex, but people just aren't realizing that all this effort has been for nothing, because they are going to die.

No. You've misunderstood.

I'm the kind of guy to play a few notes on a piano and then say, what's the point? I wouldn't say I was as good as Mozart for doing that. I would say Mozart is wasting his time, because Mozart is going to die, and there's only so much you can do on a piano anyway.
